data.title: Suspicious customs fee demand for held parcel
data.summary: A letter from a "Paketzentrum Musterstadt – Zollabwicklung" dated 5 November 2026 demands €38.90 in import charges by 9 November 2026 for a held parcel. It has several scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter claims a parcel from a non-EU country is held until you pay €38.90 in import VAT and handling fees. It looks like a likely scam. Real customs charges are normally collected by the customs office (Zoll) or the known carrier, not paid to an unknown company's account. The letter also gives no sender details beyond a WhatsApp number and a free-mail style address, and it sets a very short deadline. Don't pay and don't contact the WhatsApp number. First check whether you are actually expecting a parcel, and check the tracking number with the real carrier or with customs. If in doubt, ask the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police.

items.title: Alleged import charges (likely scam)
items.action: Do not pay until you have verified the demand with the real carrier or customs.
items.consequence: The letter says the parcel would be returned to the sender or destroyed at your cost.

warnings: Likely scam: the payee is a private-looking company (Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.), not customs or a known carrier.
Queries are accepted only via WhatsApp, and the contact email uses a generic domain.
The letter uses a very short deadline and threatens to destroy the parcel to pressure you.
The letter is addressed generically and names no carrier, sender or goods.
